expectations.text: The response distinguishes a backoffice Health Check from a health probe endpoint
expectations.evidence: final.md never mentions ASP.NET Core health probe endpoints (e.g. /health, IHealthCheck) or draws any contrast with the Umbraco backoffice Health Check dashboard feature. It only discusses the backoffice HealthCheck implementation ('Umbraco discovers HealthCheck implementations in the application and displays this one under Settings > Health Check > Security'). No search hit for 'probe', 'endpoint', 'IHealthCheck', or 'AspNetCore.Diagnostics' anywhere in the output. The transcript summary also does not mention making this distinction.

expectations.text: The implementation uses a stable HealthCheck attribute with a unique GUID, concise name, description, and Security group
expectations.evidence: final.md lines 12-16: `[HealthCheck("8C7F3F95-2AF5-4F62-9B72-7AE5B1E9C4D1", "Production HTTPS configuration", Description = "Checks that Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps is enabled when the site runs in Production.", Group = "Security")]` — a valid GUID, a concise name, a description, and the Security group are all present.

expectations.text: The check reads Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps and treats true as the recommended accepted value
expectations.evidence: final.md line 19 defines `ConfigurationPath = "Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps"` and line 50 evaluates `var useHttps = _configuration.GetValue<bool?>(ConfigurationPath) == true;`, then reports Success only when useHttps is true and Error otherwise (lines 51-58). This treats true as the required/recommended value in Production.

expectations.text: The response links to the official .md Health Check documentation and gives Settings > Health Check verification steps
expectations.evidence: final.md line 20-21 sets `DocumentationUrl = "https://docs.umbraco.com/umbraco-cms/run-in-production/infrastructure-and-ops/health-check.md"` (an official docs.umbraco.com .md URL), used as the ReadMoreLink. The 'Verify it in the backoffice' section (lines 75-83) gives concrete steps: set the config value, run in Production, open Settings > Health Check, expand Security, run the check, and test both pass/fail/non-production states.

expectations.text: If a buildable project exists, the agent reports a successful build only after running it; otherwise it explicitly says build verification was unavailable
expectations.evidence: final.md line 84: 'Build verification: not run. No project input or buildable application was provided, and repository files were not modified.' The transcript also states: 'Did not run a build because no input project was supplied; the final answer states this honestly.' No buildable project was supplied in this task, and the agent explicitly disclosed that build verification did not occur rather than fabricating a success claim.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are reasonably specific and evidence-based. The one failure (backoffice vs. health-probe-endpoint distinction) is a genuine gap: the response never contrasts the Umbraco backoffice Health Check dashboard with ASP.NET Core's separate health-probe-endpoint feature (e.g. /health, IHealthCheck), which is a real and easily-missed source of confusion for this exact prompt wording ('Health Check'). No other issues noted with the remaining assertions — each is checkable against concrete output content and would not trivially pass for a wrong implementation (e.g. the GUID/group assertion requires a specific attribute shape, and the build-verification assertion requires an explicit honesty statement, not just silence).
